text:
jen_support: customer reports intermittent failures from embeddings endpoint — sometimes we return 1536-d vectors, sometimes 1024. affects downstream indexing, billing spikes. stack: hosted API, model pinned to `semantics-1024-v1` in their app but logs show `semantics-1536-fallback` on some requests. can we triage?

mike_ml: can you paste the request headers + a sample request_id/trace id? also any SDK version? dim mismatch usually means a model-routing fallback or wrong model variant returned.

jen_support: pasted anonymized log snippet: 
```
request_id=rid_0ab12c
model_requested=semantics-1024-v1
model_served=semantics-1536-fallback
X-Embedding-Dim=1536
status=200
latency_ms=120
```
sdk: node 4.1.0, they call batch of 50 texts, no explicit model override. customer says spike correlates with a scaling window.

carlos_sre: interesting — scaling window could trigger smart-routing to a different capacity pool that only has a 1536 variant, fallback policy might map to the nearest-compatible model which has a different dim. do we have trace for `rid_0ab12c`? we need per-request route decisions.

jen_support: observability_bot returned this trace id: `trace:tr_20250312_7f9b` (attached). grabbing per-span breakdown now.

observability_bot: span breakdown for trace:tr_20250312_7f9b -> [client_send 3ms, gateway_routing 12ms, model_lookup 6ms, batch_aggregation 8ms, forward_inference 78ms, postproc 5ms, response 8ms]. route_policy used: `latency_then_cost`. fallback_reason: `model_variant_unavailable` in region `us-west-2`.

mike_ml: that lines up. root cause likely routing to a different model family during a burst. Two quick things: 1) confirm the customer's pinned version semantics-1024-v1 is provisioned in their Dedicated/Private config or allowed in Hosted routing; 2) check batching behavior — large batch size can hit pools that prefer higher-dim variants for throughput.

marie_prod: added: customers with strict embedding dims should pin exact model id and enable `strict_model_match=true` (platform setting). if they can't, we should surface a metric/alert when model_served != model_requested.

jen_support: customer asked how to reproduce locally. gave them this curl (anonymized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" 
  -H "X-Enable-Tracing: 1" 
  -d '{"model":"semantics-1024-v1","input":["one","two",...],"batch_size":50}'
```
they ran it and got mixed dims on repeated runs.

carlos_sre: reproduce steps: run looped calls with small pauses, collect `X-Trace-Id` from responses, then lookup `route_decision` in traces. also try with `batch_size=1` to see if batching is the factor. if single-item always returns 1024, then batch routing is the trigger.

mike_ml: for observability — share this set of dashboards/panels: 
- Embeddings ▸ per-route model_served / model_requested ratio (use route tag)
- Embeddings ▸ batch_size vs model_variant heatmap
- Traces ▸ route_decision waterfall (gateway -> router -> pool)
Also enable `detailed-routing` sampling at 10% for that org so we get richer traces without full sampling cost.

jen_support: customer asking for immediate mitigation — suggested options: 
1) set `strict_model_match=true` in their project settings (blocks fallbacks)
2) lower batch_size to avoid pooling into specialized queues
3) request a Dedicated reservation for semantics-1024-v1 in us-west-2 (guaranteed variant)

marie_prod: i've created a product ticket to expose a UI alert when model mismatch happens and to add a one-click `enforce-strict-match` toggle.

deploy-bot: canary deploy `router-fallback-fix v2.14` started at 2025-03-12T17:22Z — will adjust variant selection heuristics during autoscale.

mike_ml: final suggested debug steps for support to run with customer: 
- run 10 requests with `batch_size=1` (collect traces)
- run 10 requests with `batch_size=50`
- compare `model_served` in traces and `X-Embedding-Dim` header in responses
- if mismatch persists with batch_size=1, escalate to oncall routing team (cc @carlos_sre)

jen_support: customer ran 1..50 tests, confirmed batch_size=1 always 1024, batch_size=50 ~40% 1536. sending results and trace ids. thanks team, will follow up after router-fix canary stabilizes. :thumbsup:

carlos_sre: i'll watch the canary and surface any regressions. if we still see mismatches after rollout we'll open a high-priority incident.

jen_support: closing loop — customer accepted temporary mitigation (lower batch size) and will enable strict_model_match. leaving doc links: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/embeddings and https://internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/embeddings-routing-triage
